## Separate evidence layers

1. `gpui-template-lowering.test.ts` parses real source and calls the actual GPUI emitter. It checks emitted-source structure, checked-IR native parameters, lexical capture, callable identity/ABI, slot validation, actual fixture loading and ordinary setup-result adaptation. These are not Rust runtime tests. Frontend rejection of an unannotated helper formal remains a negative control, rather than a fabricated successful native source fixture.
2. `snapshot.rs` defines SDK-level native-factory checks: primitive and array identity, callable capture, invalid child values, nested/aliased slot count, external-slot validation, requested projection and failed-projection preservation. The new failed-projection check also requires restoration of the previous owner phase; it remains unexecuted.
3. `consumer.rs` imports `generated_gpui_component::CompiledComponent` and an ordinary GPUI `Entity`/`AnyView`. A real `TestAppContext` window is intended to verify native children, three repaint cycles without authored projection, state changes without update intent, one requested projection, stale commit rejection, atomic invalid-slot rejection and terminal cleanup. It does not start a Node peer or replace the generated owner.

`NativeSnapshot` is a trusted native-consumer API with public Rust fields. Its slot guard checks the validity and slot-count metadata produced by the normal constructors; it is not a security validator for an adversarial caller that manually fabricates fields or closures. The text constructor rejects boolean and undefined values rather than coercing them into accepted text children.

### Additional admitted-record boundary

Independent static review found that existing source admission permits a `module-config` record to retain native child values even when the record itself is not render output. The new source controls therefore retain local and nested records, alias/per-construction identity, captured/factory returns, field evaluation order, mixed native/state-only layouts, callable identity and factory transport. Explicit checked-IR controls cover a module-config formal/result, both orders of native/state-only calls and omitted optional arguments. They do not invent a frontend annotation or a permitted module-config property read.

A raw renderer record result is emitted but remains invalid children: the test requires its actual call once and a selected-result invalid marker, not an unsupported diagnostic relabelled as implemented behavior. The intended finite Rust record sum retains typed native fields and ownership without `Any`, a generic Value-boxed snapshot or a semantic template interpreter. Two further checked-IR cases share the same identity helper between setup ordinary configuration and render native records; flat and nested ordinary configuration must remain usable by `focus.configure`, and aliases retain identity. Four legal public component-name cases (`NativeRecordValue`, `NativeRecord0`, `NativeSnapshot`, `NativeCallable`) require private record names and fully qualified native ABI types, not a new name rejection. Four more parameterized cases cover record versus native snapshot/callable, both equality operators and both operand orders. They retain the exact two-temporary, left-first, once-only source oracle even where the semantic comparison result is statically false. One explicit checked-IR case then covers a nested helper capturing its outer module-config formal, both call orders and a same-spelled ordinary caller local. It must validate before emission; it is not a claim that an unannotated frontend formal is accepted. These twenty-five cases have now run as TypeScript emitter/source-structure controls, but they are not proof that their generated crates compile or preserve runtime ownership. Their actual generated graphs must join the later native compilation/behavior matrix; the one composed consumer does not cover them all.

The source-case recorder is an optional evidence sink only. Set `PUI_GPUI_EMISSION_ARTIFACTS` to a fresh, existing, real absolute directory per subject/run. It preserves the full input before emission, the after-input hash, the returned graph/diagnostics or thrown error, exact emitter options and their before/after hashes, and uses exclusive file writes. It never selects different product semantics or runs Cargo. An emitter throw still fails its test. Preserve original stdout/stderr in addition to receipts.
